blacklistabilityReview.evidence: 2026-07-30 re-review of both material deployments (Ethereum block 25648302, Sonic block 76778912). scUSD is the immutable Veda BoringVault share token at 0xd3dce716f3ef535c5ff8d041c1a41c3bd89b97ae on Ethereum and Sonic (owner()=0; authority=RolesAuthority 0x7D5f6108e23c0CB2cfD744E5c46f1aAfFc30A348). transfer/transferFrom call BeforeTransferHook; on both chains hook() returns the LayerZeroTeller 0x358CFACf00d0B4634849821BB3d1965b472c776a. That Teller bytecode and the public TellerWithMultiAssetSupport source expose denyAll/denyFrom/denyTo/denyOperator (requiresAuth) and beforeTransfer(from,to,operator), which reverts TransferDenied for deny-listed parties and SharesAreLocked during any share-lock window. shareLockPeriod()=0 and isPaused()=false at observation; deny calls from unprivileged callers revert UNAUTHORIZED, so activation is gated by RolesAuthority grants under chain-specific 4/6 Veda/Paladin Safe + one-day TimelockController paths documented in mintAuthority. Failure domain: Veda/Paladin RolesAuthority+Teller deny surface on each chain, plus LayerZero share routing. Upstream USDC/USDT/DAI/GHO freeze exposure remains via reserves and is not the token-level control path. Direct holder freeze/blacklistability is therefore true, not merely possible.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: scUSD is reviewed as a Sonic/Ethereum Rings asset whose architecture includes cross-chain components: underlying capital is bridged through the Sonic bridge and vault shares can be bridged through LayerZero. Because holder-facing supply can depend on bridge/vault-share routing, Pharos scores the route as external lock/mint.
